changes: p1 Jagadīśa: role changed from author+commentator to commentator only. The text is his vyākhyā on Raghunātha's Anumānamaṇidīdhiti.
purpose: rephrased as a dedication to Viśveśvara. It is not a statement of whom the copy was made for.
notes: added the doubtful 'garbhākṛtānusiṃhādyair' (perhaps 'garbhīkṛtā nṛsiṃhādyair') and other possible readings of 'jyogaḥ'.

notes: The colophon is undated. The names at the end (Rāma, Kṛṣṇa, Rāmacandra, Viśvanātha, Hiraṃvū = Heramba?) are invocations of deities, not persons. 'bhairavanāthabrāhmaṇajyogaḥ' looks corrupt. It may be a Sanskritised form of Nepali 'brāhmaṇa jyū ko' ('of Bhairavanātha brāhmaṇa-jī'), or perhaps 'brāhmaṇena'. Either way Bhairavanātha is the scribe, which agrees with the catalogue. In the verse, 'garbhākṛtānusiṃhādyair' is probably 'garbhīkṛtā nṛsiṃhādyaiḥ' ('incorporating [the views of] Nṛsiṃha and others'). That would point to earlier scholars, not to anyone involved in this copy, so no person record is made for them. 'āditaḥ paṃcalakṣaṇī' describes the portion covered: from the beginning up to the Pañcalakṣaṇī section. Raghunātha, author of the Dīdhiti, is not named; the Dīdhiti appears only as a title.
